additional_info.body:
HI Support,
We have seen a hard limitation in charging current at SID in customer project. SID is limiting the charging to 100A both outlets in parallel, first case (vehicle can not be root cause). additional_info.subject: RE: ID0395699-DC/Si-D/DE-[MP / S0 170004167] Charger power limitation issue. CRM:00643001165
additional_info.body:
Hi Benjamin,
Greetings of the day!
We have analyzed the logs for the specific date and time you provided, and we appreciate you sharing the precise details, as it has helped us analyze the logs more efficiently. The log snapshots I’ve shared below show that the EV functions as the Master, while the charger functions as the Slave. The charger provided the current and voltage that the EV demanded.
As observed in the multiple session logs, the EV's target current changed, and the EVSE current adjusted accordingly. EV charging operates on the principles of Constant Current (CC) and Constant Voltage (CV). Initially, the EV charges up to 80% State of Charge (SOC) using CC, and then it gradually switches to CV mode based on the EV's requirements. During this phase, the EV's target current decreases to protect the battery from thermal runaway and to ensure proper cell balancing.
It is charging, but at a very low power, which is causing it to take much longer, since the EV is not adjusting the current and is sticking to 100A. As you can see, the EV's SOC is changing, but very slowly.
Charger : bucVuF
Charger : BAobBx
Based on this analysis, we conclude that there is no issue with the EVSE. I hope this resolves your concerns. If you have no further questions, may we proceed with closing this ticket?
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shrey

additional_info.subject: AW: ID0395699-DC/Si-D/DE-[MP / S0 170004167] Charger power limitation issue. CRM:00643001165
additional_info.body:
Hi,
thanks for detailed explanation.
I am a little bit skeptical about that because there are two different vehicles with 19% SOC and 50%SOC limiting both to exactly 100A?
And why is EVSE_MaxCur then set to 100A as well. Charger could offer more and giving 100A in CC mode via EVSE_NowCurr?
Or is it the case that in CC the values of: EVSE_MaxCur= EVSE_NowCurr=EV_TarCur?
Where do you see that charger operates in CC or CV mode?
Would you say that this type of vehicle is always charging in CC until 80%SOC and charging in CV after 80% SOC?
I am also wondering, if you check the charging session after the mentioned one of bucVuF, we unplugged the vehicle and plugged it again. Then vehicle was charging with full power. So, why should vehicle jump to much higher current demand after re-plug? But maybe better example see below…
Please see also log below from BAobBx, charging at fix 100A, then the Charger starts to increase EVSE_MaxCurr and after that vehicle set higher target! And see second screenshot at same charging session, there is a clear limitation from EV. This two sequences does contradict your statements that vehicle is limiting factor in the “100A case”, agree?
Appreciate your feedback!
BR Benjamin

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: ID0395699-DC/Si-D/DE-[MP / S0 170004167] Charger power limitation issue. CRM:00643001165
additional_info.body:
Hi Benjamin,
Please find the reponses to the questions asked.
I am a little bit skeptical about that because there are two different vehicles with 19% SOC and 50%SOC limiting both to exactly 100A? :
It happens quite often with EVs that the continuous current demand for the charging session is limited.
And why is EVSE_MaxCur then set to 100A as well. Charger could offer more and giving 100A in CC mode via EVSE_NowCurr? :
The charger can deliver more current only if the EV demands it. Since the EV is demanding 100A, the charger does not increase its power. If there is parallel charging, the charger will automatically reduce the power on one outlet and increase it on the other.
Or is it the case that in CC the values of: EVSE_MaxCur= EVSE_NowCurr=EV_TarCur? :
No
Where do you see that charger operates in CC or CV mode?
The CC and CV modes I explained in my previous email represent the ideal way of charging any EV in the mobility business. The percentage should vary accordingly, but the ideal condition is 80%. This is theoretical, not practical.
Would you say that this type of vehicle is always charging in CC until 80%SOC and charging in CV after 80% SOC? I
can't comment on it, as it varies from vehicle to vehicle, battery SOC, and the ambient temperature inside and outside the EV.
I am also wondering, if you check the charging session after the mentioned one of bucVuF, we unplugged the vehicle and plugged it again. Then vehicle was charging with full power. So, why should vehicle jump to much higher current demand after re-plug? But maybe better example see below… :
After re-plugging, the increased current demand is purely from the EV side. If the EV is demanding higher current and our charger (EVSE) is delivering lower current, then that would be an issue.
Please see also log below from BAobBx, charging at fix 100A, then the Charger starts to increase EVSE_MaxCurr and after that vehicle set higher target! And see second screenshot at same charging session, there is a clear limitation from EV. This two sequences does contradict your statements that vehicle is limiting factor in the “100A case”, agree?  :
If it’s a limitation from the EV side, we can’t address it. As we can see, there is no issue from the EVSE side.
Maybe you have sent two more timestamps in your previous email. I'll analyze both of them and check if there is an issue from the EVSE side or if the EVSE is delivering low power.
SID ID: bucVuF, Dec 13, 9:01 AM GMT
SID ID: BAobBx, Dec 16, 8:28 AM GMT
Please give me some time to analyze the above timestamps as well.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Shrey

additional_info.body:
Hello Benjamin,
We have identified the limitation to 100A as fault from the cooling unit. It's difficult to understand the issue because even in debug level, the logs don't provide the full information. We observed that this is affecting multiple chargers.
I reported the case to R&D and 2 tickets were opened. First one is to identify the root cause for the limitation from the cooling unit and the second one is to improve the log register in those cases.
I'm now waiting from automation team (R&D), to see what is needed from our side to fix the cooling pump.
I will reach out to you as soon as I have news. If you need additional information, fell free to reach out to me by ISP email or by teams chat.
With best regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: [Escalation needed] AW: ID0395699-DC/Si-D/DE-[MP / S0 170004167] Charger power limitation issue. CRM:00643001165
additional_info.body:
Hello Benjamin,
The issue about current limitation to 100A was fixed already on the new FW. R&D found some issues in the logic that a failure in the cooling pump would lead to a current limitation but even if the issue was not present anymore would not take out that limitation. Also, some improvement was done in the logic behind the liquid temperature readings from the cooling system and most important the new firmware have clear messages in the log reporting this current limitation reasons. That said I would suggest to close this ticket since there is no other activities needed from our side.
Let me know if we can close it or additional information is needed.
With best regards,

additional_info.body:
Hello Benjamin,
Answering to your questions,
Which is the FW version where the fix is included?
v6.1.3
Is it in same hoxfix version applied for the “stuck in preparing” issue?
No, Hotfix include TIA v4.1.22, fix is done on TIA version 4.1.23 part of the new FWv6.1.3.
How can we see which charger the hotfix has applied?
Hotfixes are only installed with RC requests. Usually R&D and ES Team share a file to track those installations.
v6.0.3-0-g215cb74 give no indication, right?
Correct, sometimes we leave a txt note on charger SCB page.
Could you please deploy the hotfix on our internal test charger ID: Ltik0e as well that we have it as a reference?
We can install the hotfix but would make sense to test v6.1.3. (Hotfix is also included here) Let me know what you prefer.
Since information is provided I think this ticket can be close. The test charger work doesn't need to be on this ticket and can be handle by TEAMS chat. I will be out until 6 of March, if you want to test this earlier check with ES team if they can do the installation otherwise I will do it on my return.
